issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() is an abstract method returning String, and the exercise text and template expect printing the returned message directly. However, the solution changes the signature to public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed() and implements FeedResponse wrappers in Seal and Pig. This return-type mismatch (String vs FeedResponse) is structural and will confuse students: they will implement messageOnFeed() returning String as instructed, while the solution and its helpers use a FeedResponse type. It also creates ambiguity about whether students should create/use a FeedResponse class and how printing should behave.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of messageOnFeed() consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) change the solution to match the specification by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String and have Pig/Seal/Goat return the plain feeding message Strings (remove FeedResponse), or (B) update the problem statement, UML, and template to document and expect a FeedResponse return type (and explain the fields of FeedResponse and how to print its message). Prefer option (A) to keep the exercise aligned with the original UML and textual instructions.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() is an abstract method returning a String, but the solution introduces a new FeedResponse type and changes the abstract signature to messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse (with subclasses returning FeedResponse). The FeedResponse class and the changed return type appear only in the solution artifact, creating a mismatch in how the same conceptual 'feeding message' entity is represented across artifacts and likely confusing students who expect to implement/see a String-returning messageOnFeed().
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of the feeding message across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/UML by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String and update Seal/Pig/Goat implementations to return String (remove or adapt FeedResponse), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to document the FeedResponse type and its purpose (so students expect and implement messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse). Prefer option A to minimize conceptual mapping burden.
